question: Would you approve this as a future episode for this channel?

cards.viewer: Parents in their 60s holding money aside to help an adult child with a first home down payment someday.
cards.decision: Give the down payment money now, or keep it in safe savings and give it in 10 years?
cards.promise: We measure how much of the same home the money still covers after 10 years in T-bills, across decades of home prices.
cards.title: Help Your Kid Buy a Home Now or in 10 Years?
cards.thumbObject: Parent handing house keys and a check to an adult child

cards.viewer: Home buyers in 2026 borrowing about $320,000 who can afford the monthly payment on a 15-year mortgage.
cards.decision: Lock in a 15-year mortgage, or take a 30-year and pay it off on a 15-year schedule?
cards.promise: Using decades of weekly mortgage rates, we put a dollar price on the flexibility of a 30-year loan paid like a 15-year loan.
cards.title: 15-Year Mortgage or a 30-Year Paid in 15? The Real Price
cards.thumbObject: House keys on tags marked 15 and 30

cards.viewer: Buyers in 2026 whose mortgage payment would take 35% of gross pay, counting on raises to make it comfortable.
cards.decision: Stretch to the house at 35% of pay, or buy a cheaper one at 28%?
cards.promise: Using decades of pay history, we measure how long raises have actually taken to shrink a fixed payment from 35% to 28% of pay.
cards.title: Stretching to 35% of Your Pay: How Long Until It's 28%?
cards.thumbObject: Mortgage bill pinned under a paycheck with a stretched rubber band

cards.viewer: People in their 50s with pre-tax IRA savings and lower-income years before retirement.
cards.decision: Should you convert pre-tax IRA money to Roth IRA before retirement?
cards.promise: We simulate tax paths to see when conversions help, hurt, or mainly move taxes around.
cards.title: Roth Conversion Window: Real or Mirage?

cards.viewer: People with an old 401(k) from a former employer and a new workplace plan.
cards.decision: Should you roll the old 401(k) into an IRA or the new 401(k)?
cards.promise: We compare fees, fund menus, and taxes across real plans to show how the rollover changes outcomes.
cards.title: Old 401(k): IRA or New 401(k)?

cards.viewer: Workers in their 20s in the 22% tax bracket keeping $7,500 of savings in cash, with no retirement account yet.
cards.decision: Keep that $7,500 of cash in a Roth IRA, or in a regular savings account?
cards.promise: We run decades of actual short-term interest rates and prices to measure what the tax on interest took from cash savers, and what sheltering kept.
cards.title: Cash in a Roth IRA vs a Savings Account: Does Tax Matter?
cards.thumbObject: a glass jar of cash with coins slipping through a crack

cards.viewer: Investors in the 24% federal tax bracket buying 10-year TIPS with money that sits outside their retirement accounts.
cards.decision: Hold 10-year TIPS in a taxable brokerage account, or only inside an IRA?
cards.promise: We replay every past purchase month to measure what yearly tax on inflation adjustments left a 24% bracket holder in real, after-tax terms.
cards.title: TIPS in a Taxable Account: Still Inflation-Proof?
cards.thumbObject: an inflation-shield bond with a tax bill cutting through it

cards.viewer: Workers in the 12% tax bracket who have a 401(k) but no emergency savings and just got a surprise $1,000 bill.
cards.decision: Take a $1,000 emergency withdrawal from my 401(k), or put the bill on a credit card?
cards.promise: Using decades of actual card interest rates, we find how long a card balance can linger before its interest outweighs the tax on the withdrawal.
cards.title: $1,000 Emergency: Tap the 401(k) or Use the Card?
cards.thumbObject: a credit card and a retirement piggy bank on a balance scale

cards.viewer: Married couples earning about $130,000 combined from their jobs who are thinking about buying their first rental property.
cards.decision: Buy a rental counting on its paper losses to lower our tax on $130,000 of wages?
cards.promise: We trace the income line for deducting rental losses from the year it was set to today, measured against typical household incomes and prices.
cards.title: Rental Losses on $130,000 of Wages: Still Deductible?
cards.thumbObject: a small rental house beside a frozen income ruler

cards.viewer: Homeowners with a fixed mortgage who have enough cash to lower the balance but do not want to refinance.
cards.decision: Should you ask the lender for a recast or just pay extra principal?
cards.promise: We model payments, interest, liquidity, and moving risk using real mortgage terms and home-sale histories.
cards.title: Mortgage Recast vs Extra Principal

cards.viewer: First-time buyers in 2026 with a 10% down payment ready, weighing mortgage insurance against more years of renting.
cards.decision: Buy now with 10% down and pay mortgage insurance, or keep renting until we have 20%?
cards.promise: Using decades of home prices and mortgage rates, we measure how long mortgage insurance actually had to stay for buyers who put 10% down.
cards.title: 10% Down and Mortgage Insurance: How Long Did It Last?
cards.thumbObject: Small house with an insurance price tag hanging from the door

cards.viewer: Households who give to charity but usually take the standard deduction.
cards.decision: Bunch donations this tax year or spread gifts as usual?
cards.promise: We model tax bills from real households to show when gift timing changes the after-tax cost of giving.
cards.title: Should You Bunch Charitable Giving?

cards.viewer: Retirees and savers buying 5-year CDs through a brokerage account for money they will not need for years.
cards.decision: Take the 5-year CD paying 4.5% that the bank can call early, or the 4% CD it cannot call?
cards.promise: We replay decades of interest rates to see how often the bank would have called the CD and what the saver ended up earning.
cards.title: Callable CD at 4.5% or a Locked 4%? We Replayed History
cards.thumbObject: Bank vault door with a hook pulling back a CD certificate

cards.viewer: New retirees in their mid-60s with a travel fund parked in safe savings for the coming decade of trips.
cards.decision: Take the big trips in the first years of retirement, or spread them out over the next 10 years?
cards.promise: We check whether airfares and hotel prices rose faster than the travel money earned while it waited in T-bills.
cards.title: Travel Early in Retirement or Wait? The Price Test
cards.thumbObject: Retired couple with suitcases under an airport departures board

cards.viewer: Parents paying daycare through an employer that offers a dependent care FSA.
cards.decision: Use the dependent care FSA or skip it and claim the child care credit?
cards.promise: We compare real household tax bills to show when each route changes out-of-pocket child care cost.
cards.title: Dependent Care FSA or Child Care Credit?

cards.viewer: Car shoppers in 2026 financing about $35,000 over 60 months who are holding off until loan rates come down.
cards.decision: Buy the car now, or wait a year hoping for a lower loan rate?
cards.promise: Using years of bank car-loan rates and new-car prices, we test how often waiting a year actually lowered the monthly payment.
cards.title: Waiting a Year for a Lower Car Loan Rate: Does It Pay Off?
cards.thumbObject: Car key on a wall calendar beside a downward rate arrow

cards.viewer: Retirees in their 70s offered a funeral plan that locks today's prices if they pay the full amount now.
cards.decision: Pay for my funeral now at today's price, or keep that money in safe savings until it is needed?
cards.promise: We check how often money kept in T-bills grew fast enough to pay for the very same funeral years later.
cards.title: Prepay Your Funeral or Save the Money? What History Says
cards.thumbObject: Funeral home price list beside a glass jar of savings

cards.viewer: Drivers whose car lease is ending and who would need a loan to keep the car or replace it.
cards.decision: Should you buy out the lease or turn it in and finance another car?
cards.promise: We compare the paths using real used-car prices, loan terms, fees, taxes, and depreciation history.
cards.title: Lease Buyout or Finance the Next Car?
